translationRepairs: On the sixth day of the ninth month of Tianhui 1, the emperor younger brother, the Anban Bojilie, ascended the throne.
On the sixth day of the ninth month of Tianhui 1, the emperor's younger brother, the Anban Bojilie, ascended the throne.
皇弟 is a kinship designation, the emperor's younger brother; 'emperor younger brother' reads as a false compound title.
On the sixth day of the ninth month of the first year of Tianhui, the emperor younger brother, the Anban Bojilie, immediately took the imperial throne.
On the sixth day of the ninth month of the first year of Tianhui, the emperor's younger brother, the Anban Bojilie, immediately took the imperial throne.
The same 皇弟 requires a possessive kinship rendering in the literal field.

On the seventh day, the Shangjing garrison commander Shi was sent to report the event to Heaven, Earth, and the altars of soil and grain, while Xijin prefect Zongqiang made the announcement at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

On the seventh day, the Shangjing stay-behind administrator Shi was sent to report the event to Heaven, Earth, and the altars of soil and grain, while Xijin prefect Zongqiang made the announcement at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
上京留守 is the Shangjing stay-behind administrator, not a garrison commander.

Academicians of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and communication officers led the book out separately from the canopy pavilion. The Director of the Court went ahead as guide, the Vice Minister of Personnel escorted the book, and the Grand Commandant who would present it, the Director of the Secretariat who would read it, and the book-lifting officers followed behind in order.

Erudites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and communication officers led the book out separately from the canopy pavilion. The Director of the Court went ahead as guide, the Vice Minister of Personnel escorted the book, and the Grand Commandant who would present it, the Director of the Secretariat who would read it, and the book-lifting officers followed behind in order.
太常博士 is the erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, distinct from 學士 (academician).

When this was done, the Director of the Court came down and returned before the seal table. Casket bearers advanced together with the book-bearers, lifted the book casket, and set it on the cushioned table in the eastern bay of the hall, facing west.

When this was done, the Director of the Court came down and returned before the seal couch. Casket bearers advanced together with the book-bearers, lifted the book casket, and set it on the cushioned table in the eastern bay of the hall, facing west.
寶床 is the seal couch; the sentence later places the casket on 褥位案, the cushioned table.

When finished, the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices descended and returned before the seal table; the book-casket bearers advanced together with the book-bearers and the like, took up the book casket, set it on the cushioned table in the eastern bay of the hall facing west.

When finished, the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices descended and returned before the seal couch; the book-casket bearers advanced together with the book-bearers and the like, took up the book casket, set it on the cushioned table in the eastern bay of the hall facing west.
The literal field likewise misrenders 寶床 as a table rather than the seal couch.
Once the investiture rites were finished, the responsible offices arranged the imperial couch and seating for officials attending the banquet, all according to the prescribed banquet ceremony.

Once the book-and-seal presentation rites were finished, the responsible offices arranged the imperial couch and seating for officials attending the banquet, all according to the curved-banquet ceremony.
上冊寶禮 is the book-and-seal presentation, and 曲宴儀 is the named curved-banquet protocol, not a generic prescribed banquet; the pinyin parenthesis is unnecessary once the English term is restored.
Communication officers first led the acting Palace Attendant to present a memorial on the board: "The middle watch is strict."
Communication officers first led the acting Palace Attendant to present a memorial on the board: "The inner hall is under strict guard."
中嚴 is the inner-precinct security announcement paired with 外辦, not a 'middle watch'.
After presenting the cup, the chief duke returned the tray to the Xuanhui Commissioner; two gate commissioners then ushered him into the railing enclosure and called: "Bow."
When the cup had been received, the chief duke took the tray and handed it to the Xuanhui Commissioner; two gate commissioners then ushered him into the railing enclosure and called: "Bow."
After 跪進, 受爵訖 marks that the cup has been received; 執槃授 is handing the tray, not returning it after presenting.
All in attendance bowed twice; the announcer replied: "As you begin your reign and offer longevity, we inside and outside the palace celebrate together with you all."
All in attendance bowed twice; the announcer replied: "As you tread the new year and offer longevity, we inside and outside the palace celebrate together with you all."
履新上壽 is the New Year longevity toast; the following 聖節 formula confirms this is not an accession speech.
All in attendance bowed twice; the announcer replied: "As you begin your reign and offer longevity, inside and outside the palace we celebrate together with you all."
All in attendance bowed twice; the announcer replied: "As you tread the new year and offer longevity, inside and outside the palace we celebrate together with you all."
The literal field's 'begin your reign' likewise mistranslates 履新上壽.

Next they led the civil and military hundred officials from the rank leader down who should attend court, together with transport officials of the sixth rank and above; all entered from the left, reached the east of the red courtyard, bowed west, the gate officers announced, and they were again led to the red courtyard.

Next they led the civil and military hundred officials from the rank leader down who should attend court, together with prefectural and transport officials of the sixth rank and above; all entered from the left, reached the east of the red courtyard, bowed west, the gate officers announced, and they were again led to the red courtyard.
府運 names both prefectural and transport officials of the sixth rank and above, not transport officials alone.
The Ministry of Civil Appointments delegated the responsible office to set the station for proclaiming the edict slightly east to the north of the hundred officials' ranks, facing west.
The Department of State Affairs delegated the responsible office to set the station for proclaiming the edict slightly east to the north of the hundred officials' ranks, facing west.
尚書省 is the Department of State Affairs, not the Ministry of Civil Appointments (吏部).
The Ministry of Civil Appointments delegated the responsible office to set the station for proclaiming the edict slightly east to the north of the hundred officials' ranks, facing west.
The Department of State Affairs delegated the responsible office to set the station for proclaiming the edict slightly east to the north of the hundred officials' ranks, facing west.
The literal field repeats the same 尚書省 / 吏部 confusion.

Every official on duty bowed twice. The edict was handed to the chief of the Ministry of Civil Appointments, who stepped forward, tucked his tablet in his belt, knelt, and received it, then passed it to the Right Section officer. The Right Section officer tucked his tablet, knelt, and received it. The chief then withdrew his tablet, prostrated himself, rose, and returned to his place.

Every official on duty bowed twice. The edict was handed to the chief of the Department of State Affairs, who stepped forward, tucked his tablet in his belt, knelt, and received it, then passed it to the Right Section officer. The Right Section officer tucked his tablet, knelt, and received it. The chief then withdrew his tablet, prostrated himself, rose, and returned to his place.
The recipient of the edict is 尚書省長官, the chief of the Department of State Affairs.

All officials in attendance bowed twice; when finished, the edict was handed to the chief of the Ministry of Civil Appointments; he advanced slightly, tucked his tablet in his belt, knelt and received it; when finished, he passed it to the Right Section officer; the Right Section officer tucked his tablet, knelt and received it; when finished, the chief withdrew his tablet, prostrated himself, rose, withdrew, and returned to his station.

All officials in attendance bowed twice; when finished, the edict was handed to the chief of the Department of State Affairs; he advanced slightly, tucked his tablet in his belt, knelt and received it; when finished, he passed it to the Right Section officer; the Right Section officer tucked his tablet, knelt and received it; when finished, the chief withdrew his tablet, prostrated himself, rose, withdrew, and returned to his station.
The literal field likewise misidentifies 尚書省長官 as a Ministry of Civil Appointments chief.

The gate officer handed the amnesty edict to the Ministry's chief clerk, who knelt to receive it. He and two Ministry clerks then jointly carried it up to the reading desk and read it aloud while every official on duty knelt to listen. When the reading was finished, the edict was placed on the table and the chief clerk returned to his place.

The gate officer handed the amnesty edict to the chief clerk of the Department of State Affairs, who knelt to receive it. He and two Department of State Affairs clerks then jointly carried it up to the reading desk and read it aloud while every official on duty knelt to listen. When the reading was finished, the edict was placed on the table and the chief clerk returned to his place.
尚書省都事 and 尚書省令史 belong to the Department of State Affairs, not a ministry; the proposed noun-adjunct 'Department of State Affairs chief clerk' is accurate but awkward.

The gate officer took the amnesty edict and handed it to the chief clerk of the Ministry of Civil Appointments; the chief clerk knelt and received it; together with two Ministry clerks they jointly held it, ascended together to the reading desk and read it; all officials in attendance knelt and listened; when the reading was finished, the amnesty edict was placed on the table and the chief clerk returned to his station.

The gate officer took the amnesty edict and handed it to the chief clerk of the Department of State Affairs; the chief clerk knelt and received it; together with two Department of State Affairs clerks they jointly held it, ascended together to the reading desk and read it; all officials in attendance knelt and listened; when the reading was finished, the amnesty edict was placed on the table and the chief clerk returned to his station.
The literal replacement correctly restores 尚書省 for both the chief clerk and the two clerks.

In the outer prefectures, when the Ministry dispatched an officer to deliver the amnesty edict to the capital prefecture or a military commissioner, he sent word ahead; the chief officer then led his subordinates, clerks, and attendants out five li with banners, music, a decorated carriage, and an incense carriage to welcome him.

In the outer prefectures, when the Department of State Affairs dispatched an officer to deliver the amnesty edict to the capital prefecture or a military commissioner, he sent word ahead; the chief officer then led his subordinates, clerks, and attendants out five li with banners, music, a decorated carriage, and an incense carriage to welcome him.
The dispatching office is 尚書省, the Department of State Affairs, not a generic ministry.

In outer prefectures, when the Ministry of Civil Appointments dispatched an officer to deliver the amnesty edict to the capital prefecture or a military commissioner, he first sent someone ahead to report; the chief officer then led his subordinates, clerks, and attendants, prepared banners, music, a decorated carriage, and an incense carriage, and went to welcome them five li outside.

In outer prefectures, when the Department of State Affairs dispatched an officer to deliver the amnesty edict to the capital prefecture or a military commissioner, he first sent someone ahead to report; the chief officer then led his subordinates, clerks, and attendants, prepared banners, music, a decorated carriage, and an incense carriage, and went to welcome them five li outside.
The literal field likewise misrenders 尚書省 as the Ministry of Civil Appointments.
